translations.literal: if for these three services they are unwilling to accept replacement, follow their wish.
translations.idiomatic: those unwilling to accept these three posts may decline.

sentences.zh: 壯丁元不敷雇直處，聽如其舊。

translations.literal: Where strong youths originally paid no hire wages, permit them to follow the old practice.
translations.idiomatic: Strong youths in districts that never paid hire wages may follow old practice.

sentences.zh: 承帖雇錢許以舊寬剩錢通融支募，如土俗有不願就保正長雇役者，許募本土有產稅戶，使為耆長、壯丁以代之。

translations.literal: Warrant-bearers' hire money is permitted to use old surplus funds flexibly for recruitment; if local custom has those unwilling to accept security chief and head hiring, permit recruiting native households with tax property to serve as village elders and strong youths in their place.
translations.idiomatic: Warrant-bearers' wages may draw on old surplus funds; where locals refuse security chief and head hiring, propertied natives may be recruited as village elders and strong youths instead.

sentences.zh: 其所雇耆、戶長，已立法不得抑勒矣，若保正、長不願就雇而輒差雇者，從徒二年坐罪。”

translations.literal: For hired village and household heads, the law already forbids coercion; if security chiefs and heads are unwilling to accept hiring yet are forcibly assigned and hired, punish with two years penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Coercion of hired village and household heads is already forbidden; forcibly hiring security chiefs and heads against their will carries two years' penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 詔皆從之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark Edicts all followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark The court approved all proposals.

sentences.zh: 三年，左正言孫諤言：“役法之行，在官之數，元豐多，元祐省，雖省未嚐廢事，則多不若省；

translations.literal: In the third year, Left Rectifier Sun E said: "In implementing the service law, the number in office—Yuanfeng had more, Yuanyou reduced; although reduced, affairs were never abandoned, so more is not as good as less;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, left rectifier Sun E said: "Under the service law, Yuanfeng employed more officials and Yuanyou fewer; yet work was never neglected—fewer is better than more;

sentences.zh: 雇役之直，元豐重，元祐輕，雖輕未嚐不應募，則重不若輕。

translations.literal: hire wages—Yuanfeng was heavy, Yuanyou light; although light, recruitment was never unmet, so heavy is not as good as light.
translations.idiomatic: hire wages were higher under Yuanfeng and lower under Yuanyou; yet recruitment never failed—lighter is better than heavier.

sentences.zh: 今役法優下戶使弗輸，而盡取諸上戶，意則美矣，而法未善也。

translations.literal: The present service law favors lower households so they do not pay, while taking entirely from upper households—the intent is beautiful, but the law is not yet good.
translations.idiomatic: The present law exempts lower households while taxing upper households entirely—the intent is noble, but the method is flawed.

sentences.zh: 夫先帝建免役之法，而熙寧、元豐有異論，元祐有更變，正惟不能無弊爾。

translations.literal: The late emperor established the exemption-from-service law, and Xining and Yuanfeng had differing opinions; Yuanyou had further changes—precisely because flaws cannot be absent.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor established exemption-from-service, debated under Xining and Yuanfeng, and altered under Yuanyou—because no law is without flaws.

sentences.zh: 願無以元豐、元祐為間，期至於均平便民而止。

translations.literal: We wish not to take Yuanfeng and Yuanyou as a divide, but expect only to reach balance and convenience for the people and stop.
translations.idiomatic: Do not divide Yuanfeng from Yuanyou; seek only fairness and convenience for the people.

sentences.zh: 則善矣。”

translations.literal: Then it is good.
translations.idiomatic: That would be best.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士蔡京言：“諤之論多省、輕重，明有抑揚，謂元豐不若元祐明矣。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark Hanlin academician Cai Jing replied: "Sun E's praise of Yuanyou's lighter, smaller system clearly favors Yuanyou over Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark Hanlin academician Cai Jing replied: "Sun E's praise of Yuanyou's lighter, smaller system clearly favors Yuanyou over Yuanfeng.

sentences.zh: 諤於陛下追紹之日，敢為此言，臣竊駭之。

translations.literal: On the day Your Majesty pursues succession, E dares speak thus—I privately am astonished.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Your Majesty restores the old policies, he dares say this—I am astonished.

sentences.zh: 免役法復行將及一年，天下吏習而民安之，而諤指以為弊，則所詆者熙寧、元豐也。

translations.literal: The exemption-from-service law has been restored for nearly a year; officials throughout the realm are practiced and the people at peace, yet E points to it as flawed—then what he slanders is Xining and Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: The exemption law has been restored nearly a year; officials are practiced and the people at peace, yet Sun E calls it flawed—slandering Xining and Yuanfeng.

sentences.zh: 且元豐，雇法也；

translations.literal: Moreover, Yuanfeng is the hiring law;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfeng is the hiring system;

sentences.zh: 元祐，差法也，雇與差不可並行。

translations.literal: Yuanyou is the rotational-assignment law—hiring and rotation cannot be practiced together.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou is rotational assignment—hiring and rotation cannot coexist.

sentences.zh: 元祐固嚐兼雇，已紛然無紀矣，而諤欲不間熙、祐，是欲伸元祐之奸，惑天下之聽。”

translations.literal: Yuanyou indeed once combined hiring, already chaotic without order, yet E wishes not to distinguish Xining and Yuanyou—this is wishing to extend Yuanyou's treachery and confuse the realm's listeners.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou once mixed hiring with rotation into chaos, yet Sun E would blur Xining and Yuanyou—extending Yuanyou's treachery to confuse the realm.

sentences.zh: 詔罷諤正言，黜知廣德軍。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark An edict dismissed E from rectifier rank and demoted him to prefect of Guangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark Sun E was dismissed as rectifier and demoted to prefect of Guangde Army.

sentences.zh: 後又詔：“諸縣無得以催稅比磨追甲頭、保長，無得以雜事追保正、副。

translations.literal: Later another edict stated: "All counties may not, for urging tax collection and comparison grinding, pursue cell heads and security heads, nor may they pursue security chiefs and deputies for miscellaneous matters.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict forbade counties to summon cell heads and security heads for tax grinding or security chiefs for miscellaneous duties.

sentences.zh: 在任官以承帖為名、占破當直者，坐贓論。

translations.literal: Incumbent officials who under the name of warrant-bearers occupy and break regular duty posts shall be judged under embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: Incumbent officials who occupy regular posts under the name of warrant-bearers shall be judged for embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 所管催督租賦，州縣官輒令陪備輸物者，以違製論。”

translations.literal: For rent and tax they supervise and urge—if prefecture and county officials abruptly order them to accompany and supply goods for delivery, judge under violation of regulations.
translations.idiomatic: If prefectural officials force them to deliver goods when supervising tax collection, punish under violation of regulations.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以常平、免役、農田、水利、保甲，類著其法，總為一書，名《常平免役敕令》，頒之天下。

translations.literal: That year, Ever-Normal Granary, exemption-from-service, farmland, water conservancy, and security-chief regulations were classified and compiled into one book, named Statutes and Orders on Ever-Normal Granary and Exemption from Service, and promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: That year regulations on Ever-Normal Granary, exemption, farmland, waterworks, and security forces were compiled into the Statutes on Ever-Normal Granary and Exemption from Service and promulgated empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 詔翰林學士承旨兼詳定役法蔡京依舊詳定重修敕令。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hanlin Academician and Concurrent Service-Law Reviewer Cai Jing to follow the old practice and review and revise statutory compilations in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing, Hanlin academician and service-law reviewer, was ordered to revise the statutory compilation.

sentences.zh: 侍御史董敦逸言：“京在元祐初知開封府，附司馬光行差法，祥符一縣，數日間差至一千一百人。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Dong Dunyi said: "Jing, in early Yuanyou as prefect of Kaifeng, attached himself to Sima Guang in implementing rotational assignment—in Xiangfu County, within several days assignment reached eleven hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: Attending censor Dong Dunyi said: "In early Yuanyou Cai Jing, as Kaifeng prefect, followed Sima Guang's rotational assignment—in Xiangfu County alone eleven hundred men were assigned within days.

sentences.zh: 乞以役法專委戶部。”

translations.literal: We beg that the service law be entrusted solely to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Entrust the service law solely to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 詔令疏析。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark An edict ordered detailed memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark The court ordered a detailed response.

sentences.zh: 京奏上，復令敦逸自辨，京無責焉。

translations.literal: Jing memorialized upward; again Dong Dunyi was ordered to defend himself—Jing bore no blame.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing responded; Dong Dunyi was ordered to defend himself—Cai Jing was cleared.

sentences.zh: 元符二年，以蕭世京、張行為郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfu, Xiao Shijing and Zhang Xing were appointed as court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanfu, Xiao Shijing and Zhang Xing were appointed court gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 二人在元祐中，皆嚐言免役法為是，帝出其疏擢之。

translations.literal: Both men in Yuanyou had once said the exemption-from-service law was correct; the Emperor produced their memorials and promoted them.
translations.idiomatic: Both had once defended the exemption law under Yuanyou; the emperor promoted them citing their memorials.

sentences.zh: 既而詔河北東西、淮南運司，府界提點司，如人戶已嚐差充正夫，其免夫錢皆罷催。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered Hebei East and West and Huainan transport commissions, and the metropolitan-area supervisory commission: where households had once been assigned as regular corvée laborers, collection of exemption corvée money was all stopped.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Hebei, Huainan, and metropolitan transport offices to stop collecting corvée exemption money from households once assigned as regular laborers.

sentences.zh: 後又詔：“雖因邊事起差夫丁，須以應差雇實數上之朝廷，未得輒差。

translations.literal: Later another edict stated: "Although corvée laborers are levied because of border affairs, the actual numbers subject to assignment or hiring must be reported upward to the court; one may not assign arbitrarily.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict stated: "Even when border emergencies levy corvée labor, actual assignment and hiring numbers must be reported to the court—no arbitrary levies.

sentences.zh: 其河防並溝河歲合用一十六萬八千餘夫，聽人戶納錢以免。”

translations.literal: For river defense and annual ditch maintenance requiring more than 168,000 laborers, households are permitted to pay money to be exempt.
translations.idiomatic: The 168,000 laborers needed annually for river defense and ditch maintenance may be commuted to cash payments.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國元年，戶部奏：“京西北路鄉書手、雜職、鬥子、所由、庫秤、揀、掏之類，土人願就募，不須給之雇直，他路亦須詳度施行。”

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo, the Ministry of Revenue memorialized: "In the Jingxi North Circuit, local copyists, miscellaneous clerks, measure-bearers, runners, warehouse weighers, sorters, and carriers—natives are willing to enroll without needing hire wages paid; other circuits must also deliberate and implement in detail."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo the Ministry reported: "In the Jingxi North Circuit, locals volunteer as copyists, clerks, runners, and warehouse staff without wages; other circuits should consider the same."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark Edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark Approved.

sentences.zh: 知延安府範純粹言：“比年衙前公盜官錢，事發即逃。

translations.literal: Fan Chunzhe, prefect of Yan'an, said: "In recent years yamen-runners have openly embezzled government money; when the matter is exposed they flee at once.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chunzhe, prefect of Yan'an, said: "Yamen-runners have openly embezzled government funds and fled when exposed.

sentences.zh: 乞許輪差上等鄉戶使供衙役。”

translations.literal: We beg permission to rotate assignment of upper-rank township households to supply yamen service.
translations.idiomatic: Permit rotational assignment of upper-rank township households for yamen service.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史彭汝霖劾純粹所言有害良法，宜加黜責。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark Palace Attendant Censor Peng Rulin impeached Chunzhe's words as harming the good law and deserving demotion and censure.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark Palace attendant censor Peng Rulin impeached Fan Chunzhe for undermining the good law.

sentences.zh: 詔純粹所乞不行。

translations.literal: An edict: Chunzhe's request was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chunzhe's request was denied.

sentences.zh: 其後，知襄州俞以襄州總受他州布綱而轉致他州，是衙前重役並在一州，事理不均。

translations.literal: Later, Yu, prefect of Xiangzhou, because Xiangzhou altogether received cloth-transport quotas from other prefectures and forwarded them to other prefectures—thus yamen-runners' heavy duties were all concentrated in one prefecture, the principle uneven.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yu, prefect of Xiangzhou, noted that Xiangzhou received other prefectures' cloth-transport quotas and forwarded them onward—concentrating all yamen-runner burdens in one prefecture unfairly.

sentences.zh: 臣僚謂輒毀紹聖成法，請重黜。

translations.literal: Court officials said Yu rashly destroyed Shaosheng established law and begged heavy demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Officials accused Yu of destroying Shaosheng law and demanded heavy punishment.

sentences.zh: 坐責授散官，安置太平州。

translations.literal: Yu was punished by demotion to irregular official and assigned to Taiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was demoted to irregular rank and assigned to Taiping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 崇寧元年，尚書省言：“前令大保長催稅而不給雇直，是為差役，非免役也。”

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning, the Secretariat said: "The former order that great security heads urge tax collection without hire wages is rotational service, not exemption from service."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongning the Secretariat said: "Making great security heads collect taxes without wages is rotational service, not exemption."

sentences.zh: 詔提舉司以元輸雇錢如舊法均給。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark An edict ordered supervisory commissions to distribute originally paid hire money evenly as under the old law.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark Supervisory commissions were ordered to distribute hire money as under the old law.

sentences.zh: 永興軍路州縣官乞復行差役；

translations.literal: Yongxing Circuit prefecture and county officials begged to restore rotational assignment;
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing Circuit officials sought to restore rotational assignment;

sentences.zh: 湖南、江西提舉司以物賤乞減吏胥雇直，罷給役人雇錢，皆害法意，應改從其舊。

translations.literal: Hunan and Jiangxi supervisory commissions, because goods were cheap, begged to reduce clerks' hire wages and stop paying service personnel hire money—all harming the law's intent and should be changed back to the old practice.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan and Jiangxi commissions sought lower clerk wages and no service wages because goods were cheap—all contrary to the law and to be reversed.

sentences.zh: 詔戶部並遵奉《紹聖常平免役敕令格式》及先降《紹聖簽貼役法》，行之天下。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue all to respectfully follow the Shaosheng Statutes and Formats on Ever-Normal Granary and Exemption from Service and the previously issued Shaosheng Annotated Service Law, implementing them throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue was ordered to enforce the Shaosheng statutes and annotated service law empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 二年，臣僚言：“常平之息，歲取二分，則五年有一倍之數；

translations.literal: In the second year, court officials said: "Ever-Normal interest, taking two-tenths per year, then in five years there is a doubling;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year officials said: "Ever-Normal interest at two-tenths yearly doubles in five years;

sentences.zh: 免役剩錢，歲收一分，則十年有一年之備。

translations.literal: exemption surplus money, collecting one-tenth per year, then in ten years there is one year's reserve.
translations.idiomatic: exemption surplus at one-tenth yearly provides one year's reserve in ten.

sentences.zh: 故紹聖立法，常平息及一倍，免役寬剩及三料，取旨蠲免，以明朝廷取於民者，非以為利也。

translations.literal: Therefore Shaosheng legislation: when Ever-Normal interest reaches one doubling and exemption surplus reaches three quotas, seek imperial decree for remission, to clarify that what the court takes from the people is not suited for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Shaosheng law therefore remitted Ever-Normal interest at doubling and exemption surplus at three quotas, showing the court did not profit from the people.

sentences.zh: 而集賢殿修撰、知鄧州呂仲甫前為戶部侍郎，輒以狀申都省，乞刪去上條。”

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark But Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies and Prefect of Dengzhou Lü Zhongfu, formerly Vice Minister of Revenue, rashly memorialized the Department of State Affairs begging to delete the above article.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark But Lü Zhongfu, formerly vice minister of revenue and now prefect of Dengzhou, memorialized to delete that provision.

sentences.zh: 詔黜仲甫，落職知海州。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark An edict demoted Zhongfu, removed office, and made him prefect of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark Lü Zhongfu was demoted to prefect of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 後又詔：常平司候豐衍有餘日，具此製奏蠲之。

translations.literal: Later another edict: when the Ever-Normal commission awaits abundance with surplus days, compile this regulation and memorialize for remission.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Ever-Normal funds were abundant, commissions were to memorialize for remission under this rule.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，詔：“諸州縣召募吏人，如有非四等以上戶及在州縣五犯杖罪，悉從罷遣，不得再占諸處名役，別募三等以上人充。”

translations.literal: In the first year of Daguan, an edict stated: "In all prefectures and counties recruiting clerks, if any are not households of the fourth rank and above, or have five cane punishments in prefecture and county, all dismiss and do not permit again occupying name-service elsewhere; separately recruit men of the third rank and above."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daguan an edict stated: "Recruited clerks not of fourth rank or above, or with five prefectural cane convictions, shall be dismissed and never reappointed; recruit third rank and above instead."

sentences.zh: 於是舊胥既盡罷，而弊根未革，老奸巨猾，匿身州縣，舞法擾民，蓋甚前日。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark Thereupon experienced clerks were all dismissed, yet the root of abuse was not reformed—old crafty great schemers hid in prefectures and counties, manipulating law and harassing the people, probably worse than before.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark experienced clerks were dismissed, but veteran schemers hid in local government and manipulated the law worse than before.

sentences.zh: 其後，又不許上三等人戶投充弓手，所募皆浮浪，無所顧藉，盜賊公行，為害四方。

translations.literal: Later, upper-three-rank households were again not permitted to enroll as bowmen; all recruited were floating idlers without attachment; bandits walked openly, harming the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Later upper-three-rank households were barred from bowman service; recruits were drifters without local ties, and banditry spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 至是，復詔州縣募役依元豐舊法。

translations.literal: At this point, again an edict ordered prefectures and counties to recruit service according to Yuanfeng old law.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered recruitment under Yuanfeng rules again.

sentences.zh: 政和元年，臣僚言：“元豐中，鞏州歲敷役錢止四百千，今累敷至緡錢近三萬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenghe, court officials said: "In Yuanfeng, Gongzhou's assessed service money was only four hundred thousand; now cumulative assessment reaches nearly thirty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenghe officials reported: "Gongzhou's service assessment was four hundred thousand under Yuanfeng; it now nears thirty thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 又元豐八年，命存留寬剩錢毋得過二分，紹聖再加裁定，止許存留一分。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the eighth year of Yuanfeng, it was ordered that retained surplus money must not exceed two-tenths; Shaosheng again added determination, permitting only one-tenth retention.
translations.idiomatic: eighth year of Yuanfeng capped surplus at two-tenths; Shaosheng reduced it to one-tenth.

sentences.zh: 此時考詳法意，非取寬剩，遂改名準備錢，而嚴立禁約，若擅增敷歲額及樁留準備過數者，並以違製論。

translations.literal: At that time examining the law's intent in detail, not taking surplus, they then renamed it reserve funds and strictly established prohibitions: if one arbitrarily increased annual assessment or staked reserve beyond quota, all judge under violation of regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The surplus was renamed reserve funds with strict limits: unauthorized increases or excess reserves were punishable.

sentences.zh: 今乞飭提舉常平官檢察，及核究鞏州取贏之因以聞。”

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark Now we beg to order Ever-Normal supervisory officials to inspect, and investigate the cause of Gongzhou's profit and report.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark Supervisory officials were ordered to investigate Gongzhou's excess assessments.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark Approved.

sentences.zh: 宣和元年，言者謂：“役錢一事，神宗首防官戶免多，特責半輸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanhe, critics said: "On service money, Emperor Shenzong first guarded against official households' excessive exemption, especially ordering half payment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanhe critics said: "Emperor Shenzong first required official households to pay half service money to prevent excessive exemption.

sentences.zh: 今比戶稱官，州縣募役之類既不可減，雇令官戶所減之數均入下戶，下戶於常賦之外，又代官戶減半之輸，豈不重困？”

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark Now comparing households all claim official status; prefecture and county recruitment cannot be reduced, yet the amount official households reduce is averaged into lower households—lower households, beyond regular tax, also substitute for official households' half reduction—how is this not redoubled distress?
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark Now many claim official status while recruitment cannot be cut; official households' reductions are shifted to lower households, who pay regular tax plus officials' half—doubling their burden.

sentences.zh: 詔：“自今二等以上戶，因直降指揮非泛補官者，輸賦、差科、免役並不得示官戶法減免，已免者改之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark An edict stated: "From now, households of the second rank and above who through direct demotion edicts receive non-general supplemental office—tax, assignment, and exemption shall not be shown official-household law reductions; those already reduced are changed.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark Second-rank and above households receiving non-general office by demotion edict shall not claim official reductions; existing reductions are revoked.

sentences.zh: 進納人自如本法。”

translations.literal: Tribute contributors follow the original law as before.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute contributors follow the original law.

sentences.zh: 保長月給雇錢，督催稅賦。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark Security heads receive monthly hire money to supervise and urge tax collection.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark Security heads receive monthly wages to collect taxes.

sentences.zh: 比年諸縣或每稅戶一二十家，又差一人充甲頭及催稅人，十日一進，赴官比磨，求取決責，有害良民，詔禁之。

translations.literal: In recent years some counties for every ten or twenty tax households again assign one person as cell head and tax-urging person, advancing every ten days to office for comparison grinding, seeking decisive punishment—harming good commoners; edict forbade this.
translations.idiomatic: Some counties assigned one tax collector per ten or twenty households, summoning them every ten days for grinding and punishment—harming good people; forbidden by edict.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔：“州縣昨因儆察私鑄，令五家為保。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict stated: "Prefectures and counties, because of inspecting private coining, ordered five households as security groups.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year an edict noted: "Prefectures formed five-household security groups to inspect private coining.

sentences.zh: 城郭亦差坊正、副領受文書，由此追呼陪費，或析居、逃移以避差使。

translations.literal: In cities ward chiefs and deputies also received documents, and through this were summoned with accompanying expenses; some divided households or fled to avoid assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Urban ward chiefs received documents, faced summons and expenses, and some divided households or fled to avoid duty.

sentences.zh: 其所置坊正、副可罷。”

translations.literal: The ward chiefs and deputies established may be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Ward chiefs and deputies may be abolished.

sentences.zh: 自紹聖復雇役，而建炎初罷之。

translations.literal: From Shaosheng's restoration of hired service, until the beginning of Jianyan it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Hired service restored under Shaosheng was abolished at the beginning of Jianyan.

sentences.zh: 已而討論其法之不可廢也，參政李固言於高宗曰：“常平法本於漢耿壽昌，豈可以王安石而廢之？”

translations.literal: Soon discussion held that the law could not be abandoned; Participating Councilor Li Gu spoke to Emperor Gaozong, saying: "The Ever-Normal law originally derives from Han Geng Shouchang—how can it be abolished because of Wang Anshi?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon officials argued the law could not be abandoned; councilor Li Gu told Emperor Gaozong: "The Ever-Normal system derives from Han Geng Shouchang—how can it be abolished because of Wang Anshi?"

sentences.zh: 且當時招射士無以供庸直，詔官戶役錢勿減半，民戶役錢概增二分。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark Moreover, at that time recruiting archers lacked funds for corvée wages; an edict ordered official households' service money not reduced by half, and common households' service money generally increased two-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark Lacking funds for archers' wages, official households' reductions were suspended and common households' assessments raised twenty percent.

sentences.zh: 後復減之。

translations.literal: Later it was again reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Later assessments were reduced again.

sentences.zh: 兼官舊給庸錢以募戶長，及立保甲，則儲庸錢以助經費。

translations.literal: Concurrent officials formerly gave corvée money to recruit household heads; when security groups were established, corvée money was stored to help cover expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent officials once paid corvée money to recruit household heads; under security groups that money was stored for expenses.

sentences.zh: 未幾，廢保甲，復戶長，而庸錢不復給，遂為總製窠名焉。

translations.literal: Before long, security groups were abolished and household heads restored, yet corvée money was no longer paid—thus it became a comprehensive system account name.
translations.idiomatic: Security groups were soon abolished and household heads restored, but corvée money was no longer paid—it became a general revenue category.

sentences.zh: 然役起於物力，物力升降不淆，則役法公。

translations.literal: Yet service arises from material wealth; if material wealth rises and falls without confusion, then the service law is fair.
translations.idiomatic: Service arises from assessed wealth; if wealth assessments are accurate, the service law is fair.

sentences.zh: 是以紹興以來，講究推割、推排之製：凡百姓典賣產業，稅賦與物力一並推割。

translations.literal: Therefore since Shaoxing, the systems of transfer-cutting and transfer-ranking have been studied: whenever commoners mortgage or sell property, tax and material wealth are transfer-cut together.
translations.idiomatic: Since Shaoxing, transfer-cutting and transfer-ranking systems were refined: when property is sold, tax and wealth assessments transfer together.

sentences.zh: 至於推排，則因其資產之進退為之升降，三歲而一行之。

translations.literal: As for transfer-ranking, it rises and falls according to assets' advance and retreat, implemented once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Transfer-ranking adjusts assessments every three years according to changes in assets.

sentences.zh: 然當時之弊，或以小民粗有米粟，僅存室廬，凡耕耨刀斧之器，雞豚犬彘之畜，纖微細瑣皆得而籍之。

translations.literal: Yet abuses of the time included: small commoners who roughly had grain, barely preserving huts and houses—for all plowing hoes, axes, chickens, pigs, dogs, pigs, and trifling minute items, all could be registered.
translations.idiomatic: Abuses included registering every hoe, axe, chicken, and pig of households with only a little grain and a hut.

sentences.zh: 吏視賂之多寡，為物力之低昂。

translations.literal: Clerks viewed the amount of bribes as high or low for material wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks set wealth assessments according to bribes received.

sentences.zh: 上之人憂之，於是又為之限製，除質庫房廊、停塌店鋪、租牛、賃船等外，不得以豬羊雜色估計，其後並耕牛租牛以免之。

translations.literal: Superiors worried; therefore limits were again set—excluding pawnshops, corridors, transit warehouses, rented oxen, chartered boats, and the like, one may not estimate with pigs, sheep, and miscellaneous colors; later plowing oxen and rented oxen were also exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Authorities imposed limits: pawnshops, warehouses, rented oxen, and chartered boats were excluded, and later plowing and rented oxen too.

sentences.zh: 若江之東西，以畝頭計稅，亦有不待推排者。

translations.literal: In Jiang east and west, tax is calculated by mu head; some also do not await transfer-ranking.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yangzi delta, tax is calculated by mu and sometimes needs no transfer-ranking.

sentences.zh: 保正、長之立也，五家相比，五五為保，十大保為都保，有保長，有都、副保正；

translations.literal: On establishing security chiefs and heads: five households compare together, five-fives make a security group, ten great security groups make a security district, with security heads, and district chief and deputy security chiefs;
translations.idiomatic: Security chiefs and heads are organized thus: five households form a group, ten groups a district, with cell heads and district chiefs;

sentences.zh: 餘及三保亦置長，五大保亦置都保正，其不及三保、五大保者，或為之附庸，或為之均並，不一也。

translations.literal: those reaching three security groups also establish heads; five great security groups also establish district security chiefs; where not reaching three groups or five great groups, some are made dependencies or evenly merged—not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: districts with fewer than three groups or five great groups are merged or attached variably.

sentences.zh: 戶則以物力之高下為役次之久近。

translations.literal: Households then take material wealth high and low as near or far in service rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Households rotate service according to wealth, the wealthy serving less often.

sentences.zh: 若夫品官之田，則有限製，死亡，子孫減半；

translations.literal: As for ranked officials' fields, there are limits; on death, descendants halve;
translations.idiomatic: Officials' landholdings are limited; on death descendants' exemption is halved;

sentences.zh: 蔭盡，差役同編戶。

translations.literal: when hereditary privilege is exhausted, rotational service is the same as registered households.
translations.idiomatic: when hereditary privilege ends, they serve like ordinary households.

sentences.zh: 〈（一品五十頃，二品四十五頃，三品四十頃，四品三十五頃，五品三十頃，六品二十五頃，七品二十頃，八品十頃，九品五頃。）〉

translations.literal: (First rank fifty qing, second rank forty-five qing, third rank forty qing, fourth rank thirty-five qing, fifth rank thirty qing, sixth rank twenty-five qing, seventh rank twenty qing, eighth rank ten qing, ninth rank five qing.)
translations.idiomatic: (First rank fifty qing, second rank forty-five qing, third rank forty qing, fourth rank thirty-five qing, fifth rank thirty qing, sixth rank twenty-five qing, seventh rank twenty qing, eighth rank ten qing, ninth rank five qing.)

sentences.zh: 封贈官子孫差役，亦同編戶。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed and bestowed officials' descendants' rotational service is also the same as registered households.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of enfeoffed and bestowed officials serve like ordinary households.

sentences.zh: 〈（謂父母生前無官，因伯叔或兄弟封贈者。）〉

translations.literal: (Meaning: parents had no office during their lives, but enfeoffment came through uncles or brothers.)
translations.idiomatic: (Meaning: parents held no office in life, but rank was gained through enfeoffment via uncles or brothers.)

sentences.zh: 凡非泛及七色補官，不在限田免役之數；

translations.literal: All non-general and seven-color supplemental offices are not within the counted fields for limited-land service exemption;
translations.idiomatic: All non-general and seven-category supplemental offices fall outside limited-land service exemption;

sentences.zh: 其奏薦弟侄子孫，原自非泛、七色而來者，仍同差役。

translations.literal: those recommended by memorial for younger brothers, nephews, and descendants who originally came from non-general or seven-color routes still share rotational service equally.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants recommended by memorial who originally entered through non-general or seven-category routes still bear rotational service like common households.

sentences.zh: 進納、軍功、捕盜、宰執給使、減年補授，轉至升朝官，即為官戶；

translations.literal: tribute contribution, military merit, bandit capture, chancellor's attendants, and reduced-year supplemental appointment—when promoted to court-audience office, they become official households;
translations.idiomatic: Tribute contributors, military merit holders, bandit-catchers, chancellors' attendants, and reduced-year appointees who reach court audience rank become official households;

sentences.zh: 身亡，子孫並同編戶。

translations.literal: on death, descendants are all the same as registered households.
translations.idiomatic: On death, their descendants are treated like ordinary registered households.

sentences.zh: 太學生及得解及經省試者，雖無限田，許募人充役。

translations.literal: Imperial University students and those who passed prefectural or metropolitan examinations, though without limited fields, are permitted to recruit men to fill service.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial University students and examination degree-holders without limited fields may hire substitutes for service.

sentences.zh: 單丁、女戶及孤幼戶，並免差役。

translations.literal: Single-male, female-headed, and orphaned-infant households are all exempt from rotational assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Single-male, female-headed, and orphaned-infant households are exempt from rotational assignment.

sentences.zh: 凡無夫無子，則為女戶。

translations.literal: All without husbands and without sons count as female-headed households.
translations.idiomatic: A household without husband and sons is a female-headed household.

sentences.zh: 女適人，以奩錢置產，仍以夫為戶。

translations.literal: When a woman marries, dowry money is used to establish property, and the household is still registered under the husband.
translations.idiomatic: When a woman marries, dowry establishes property registered under her husband's household.

sentences.zh: 其合差保正、長，以家業錢數多寡為限，以限外之數與官、編戶輪差。

translations.literal: For assignment as security chief or head, the limit is the amount of family estate money; amounts beyond the limit rotate with official and registered households.
translations.idiomatic: Security chiefs and heads are assigned by estate size; amounts beyond the limit rotate with official and registered households.

sentences.zh: 總首、部將免保正、長差役。

translations.literal: Commanders-in-chief and unit officers are exempt from security chief and head assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders-in-chief and unit officers are exempt from security chief and head duty.

sentences.zh: 文州義士已免之田，不許典賣，老疾身亡，許承襲。

translations.literal: Exempt fields of righteous warriors in Wenzhou may not be mortgaged or sold; on old age, illness, or death, inheritance is permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Exempt fields of Wenzhou righteous warriors may not be sold; on death they may be inherited.

sentences.zh: 凡募人充役，並募土著之人，其放停兵及嚐為公人者，並不許募。

translations.literal: All who recruit men for service must recruit natives; discharged soldiers and those who have once been government runners may not be recruited.
translations.idiomatic: Recruits must be natives; discharged soldiers and former government runners may not be hired.

sentences.zh: 既有募人，官不得復追正身。

translations.literal: Once recruits exist, officials may not again pursue the person in the flesh.
translations.idiomatic: Once substitutes are hired, officials may not summon the liable household in person.

sentences.zh: 募人憑藉官勢，奸害善人，斷罪外，坐募之者。

translations.literal: If recruits rely on official power to harm good people, beyond conviction they also punish the recruiter.
translations.idiomatic: If hires abuse official power to harm the innocent, the recruiter is also punished.

sentences.zh: 高宗在河朔，親見閭閻之苦，嚐歎知縣不得人，一充役次，即便破家，是以講究役法甚便。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong, in Hebei, personally saw the suffering of lanes and alleys and once sighed that if the county magistrate were not the right man, one rotation of service would at once ruin a household; therefore he studied the service law very carefully for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: In Hebei, Emperor Gaozong saw how one bad magistrate and one service rotation could ruin a household, and therefore refined the service law with great care.

sentences.zh: 乾道五年，處州鬆陽縣倡為義役，眾出田穀，助役戶輪充，自是所在推行。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiandao, Songyang County in Chuzhou pioneered righteous service: the multitude contributed field grain to help households on rotation, and thereafter it was implemented everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qiandao, Songyang County in Chuzhou pioneered community service: neighbors pooled grain to support households on rotation, and the practice spread.

sentences.zh: 十一年，御史謝諤言：“義役之行，當從民便，其不願者，乃行差役。”

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Censor Xie E said: "The practice of righteous service should follow what the people find convenient; those unwilling should use rotational assignment."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, censor Xie E said: "Community service should follow local preference; unwilling households should use rotational assignment."

sentences.zh: 上然之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 朱熹謂義役有未盡善者四事。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi said righteous service had four matters not yet fully good.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi said community service still had four flaws.

sentences.zh: 蓋始倡義役者，惟恐議之未詳，慮之未周，而踵之者不能皆善人，於是其弊日開，其流日甚。

translations.literal: For those who first pioneered righteous service feared deliberation was not detailed and planning not thorough, while followers could not all be good men—thus abuses opened daily and the current grew daily worse.
translations.idiomatic: The pioneers feared incomplete planning, but successors were not all good men—so abuses spread daily.

sentences.zh: 或以材智把握，而專義役之利；

translations.literal: Some grasped with talent and schemes and monopolized the profit of righteous service;
translations.idiomatic: Some used clever schemes to monopolize community-service benefits;

sentences.zh: 或以氣力淩駕，而私差役之權。

translations.literal: some overawed with physical force and privately held power over rotational assignment.
translations.idiomatic: some bullied neighbors and seized control of rotational assignment.

sentences.zh: 是以虐貧優富，淩寡暴孤。

translations.literal: Thus they abused the poor and favored the rich, oppressed the few and violently harmed the solitary.
translations.idiomatic: They abused the poor, favored the rich, and bullied the weak and solitary.

sentences.zh: 義役之名立，而役戶不得以安其業；

translations.literal: When the name of righteous service was established, households on service could not settle their occupations;
translations.idiomatic: Once community service was named, service households could not live in peace;

sentences.zh: 雇役之法行，而役戶不得以安其居，信乎所謂未盡善之弊也。

translations.literal: when the law of hired service ran, households on service could not settle their dwellings—truly the so-called flaws of not yet being fully good.
translations.idiomatic: when hired service ran, they could not settle their homes—truly the flaws Zhu Xi named.

sentences.zh: 淳熙五年，臣僚奏令提舉官歲考屬邑差役當否，以詞訟多寡為殿最；

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunxi, officials memorialized ordering supervisory officials annually to examine whether subordinate counties' rotational assignment was proper, taking the amount of litigation as the criterion for excellence or failure;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chunxi, officials proposed annual review of local assignment by litigation volume;

sentences.zh: 令役戶輪管以提其役，置募人以奉官之行移，則公私便而義役立矣。

translations.literal: ordering households on service to rotate in managing to raise their service, and placing recruits to handle official documents—then public and private would be convenient and righteous service would stand.
translations.idiomatic: service households would rotate management, recruits would handle documents, and community service would work for all.

sentences.zh: 慶元二年，吏部尚書許及之因淳熙陳居仁所奏，取祖宗免役舊法及紹興十七年以後續降旨符，修為一書，名曰《役法撮要》。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingyuan, Minister of Personnel Xu Jizhi, following Chen Juren's memorial in Chunxi, took ancestral exemption laws and edicts after the seventeenth year of Shaoxing and compiled one book named Essentials of the Service Law.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qingyuan, Xu Jizhi compiled ancestral exemption laws and Shaoxing edicts into Essentials of the Service Law.

sentences.zh: 五年，書成，左丞相京鏜上之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the book was complete, Left Chancellor Han Tong presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, left chancellor Han Tong presented the completed book.

sentences.zh: 其法可以悠久，其或未久而輒弊者，人也。

translations.literal: Its law could be long-lasting; if not long-lasting and soon flawed, it was people.
translations.idiomatic: The law could endure; when it failed soon, people were to blame.

sentences.zh: 振恤水旱、蝗螟、饑疫之災，治世所不能免，然必有以待之，《周官》“以荒政十有二聚萬民”是也。

translations.literal: Relief for flood, drought, locusts, and famine epidemics—no well-governed age can avoid them, yet there must be means to await them; this is the Zhou Offices' "twelve famine policies to gather the myriad people."
translations.idiomatic: Floods, drought, locusts, and epidemics are unavoidable, but a state must prepare; this is the Zhou Offices' twelve famine policies.

sentences.zh: 宋之為治，一本於仁厚，凡振貧恤患之意，視前代尤為切至。

translations.literal: Song governance is rooted in benevolence and generosity; all intent to relieve poverty and succor disaster is more earnest than in prior ages.
translations.idiomatic: Song governance rested on benevolence; relief for the poor and afflicted was more earnest than in prior dynasties.

sentences.zh: 諸州歲歉，必發常平、惠民諸倉粟，或平價以糶，或貸以種食，或直以振給之，無分於主客戶。

translations.literal: In all prefectures when the year is lean, they surely release grain from Ever-Normal and Beneficial granaries, or sell at fair price, or lend seed food, or directly grant relief—without distinction between native and client households.
translations.idiomatic: In lean years prefectures released Ever-Normal and Beneficial granary grain, sold at fair price, lent seed, or gave direct relief to all households alike.

sentences.zh: 不足，則遣使馳傳發省倉，或轉漕粟於他路；

translations.literal: If insufficient, they dispatch messengers by post to release provincial granaries, or transfer transport grain from other circuits;
translations.idiomatic: If insufficient, they released provincial stores or transferred grain from other circuits;

sentences.zh: 或募富民出錢粟，酬以官爵，勸諭官吏，許書曆為課；

translations.literal: or recruit wealthy households to contribute money and grain, rewarding with rank and title, urging officials, and permitting record in registers for merit;
translations.idiomatic: or recruited wealthy households with rank and merit records;

sentences.zh: 若舉放以濟貧乏者，秋成，官為理償。

translations.literal: if lending to relieve the destitute, at autumn harvest the government repays on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: loans to the destitute were repaid by government at harvest.

sentences.zh: 又不足，則出內藏或奉宸庫金帛，鬻祠部度僧牒；

translations.literal: If still insufficient, they release inner palace or Palatial Treasury gold and silk, or sell Ministry diplomas for monks;
translations.idiomatic: If still insufficient, inner palace funds or monk diplomas were sold;

sentences.zh: 東南則留發運司歲漕米，或數十萬石，或百萬石濟之。

translations.literal: in the southeast they retain Transport Commission annual tribute grain, sometimes several hundred thousand or a million shi for relief.
translations.idiomatic: in the southeast, transport grain in hundreds of thousands of shi was held for relief.

sentences.zh: 賦租之未入、入未備者，或縱不取，或寡取之，或倚閣以須豐年。

translations.literal: Tax rent not yet entered or not fully entered—sometimes they forbear collection, sometimes take little, sometimes defer accounts awaiting a fertile year.
translations.idiomatic: Uncollected taxes were forborne, reduced, or deferred to fertile years.

sentences.zh: 寬逋負，休力役，賦入之有支移、折變者省之，應給蠶鹽若和糴及科率追呼不急、妨農者罷之。

translations.literal: They relax overdue obligations, rest corvée labor, reduce branch delivery and conversion of tax items due, halt silkworm salt and commissariat purchases and urgent collections harming farming.
translations.idiomatic: Overdue debts were relaxed, corvée rested, branch deliveries reduced, and harmful levies halted.

sentences.zh: 薄關市之征，鬻牛者免算，運米舟車除沿路力勝錢。

translations.literal: They lighten market-pass duties; ox sellers are exempt from assessment; rice transport carts and boats are freed from route strength money along the way.
translations.idiomatic: Market duties were lightened; ox sales and grain transport were relieved of fees.

sentences.zh: 利有可與民共者不禁，水鄉則蠲蒲、魚、果、蓏之稅。

translations.literal: Profits that may be shared with the people are not forbidden; in water districts taxes on rush, fish, fruit, and melons are remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shared profits were not forbidden; water districts' taxes on fish, fruit, and reeds were remitted.

sentences.zh: 選官分路巡撫，緩囚係，省刑罰。

translations.literal: They select officials to tour by route, easing prisoners and reducing punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Officials toured circuits, easing prisoners and reducing punishments.

sentences.zh: 饑民劫囷窖者，薄其罪；

translations.literal: Starving people who rob granaries and cellars—their crimes are lightened;
translations.idiomatic: Starving people who raided granaries received lighter sentences;

sentences.zh: 民之流亡者，關津毋責渡錢；

translations.literal: fleeing commoners—passes and fords do not charge ferry money;
translations.idiomatic: fugitives paid no ferry fees;

sentences.zh: 道京師者，諸城門振以米，所至舍以官第或寺觀，為淖糜食之，或人日給糧。

translations.literal: those reaching the capital—city gates give rice relief; along the way they lodge in government mansions or temples, are given gruel, or daily grain.
translations.idiomatic: at the capital, gates gave rice; along the road, lodging, gruel, or daily grain.

sentences.zh: 可歸業者，計日並給遣歸；

translations.literal: Those who can return to their occupations are sent home with daily provisions;
translations.idiomatic: Those who could return home were sent with daily provisions;

sentences.zh: 無可歸者，或賦以閑田，或聽隸軍籍，或募少壯興修工役。

translations.literal: those with nowhere to return—fields are assigned, or they enter military registers, or young men are recruited for construction labor.
translations.idiomatic: others received land, entered the army, or were recruited for public works.

sentences.zh: 老疾幼弱不能存者，聽官司收養。

translations.literal: The old, ill, and young unable to survive are permitted to be taken in by government offices.
translations.idiomatic: The aged, ill, and young unable to survive were taken in by government.

sentences.zh: 水災州縣具船筏拯民，置之水不到之地，運薪糧給之。

translations.literal: Flood districts prepare boats and rafts to save the people, placing them where water does not reach, transporting fuel and grain to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Flood districts used boats to rescue people and supply fuel and grain.

sentences.zh: 因饑疫若厭溺死者，官為埋祭，厭溺死者加賜其家錢粟。

translations.literal: Because of famine epidemics or drowned dead, the government buries and sacrifices; for drowned dead, families additionally receive money and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The government buried victims of famine and drowning and compensated drowned victims' families.

sentences.zh: 京師苦寒，或物價翔踴，置場出米及薪炭，裁其價予民。

translations.literal: The capital is bitterly cold, or prices soar—markets are set out with rice and fuel coal, cutting prices to give the people.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was bitterly cold or prices soared, rice and coal were sold below market price.

sentences.zh: 前後率以為常。

translations.literal: Before and after, this was always the constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: This became constant practice.

sentences.zh: 蝗為害，又募民撲捕，易以錢粟，蝗子一升至易菽粟三升或五升。

translations.literal: When locusts harm, the people are also recruited to capture them, exchanged for money and grain; one sheng of locust eggs exchanges for three or five sheng of beans and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts were fought by paying the people for captures; locust eggs were exchanged for grain.

sentences.zh: 詔州郡長吏優恤其民，間遣內侍存問，戒監司俾察官吏之老疾、罷懦不任職者。

translations.literal: Edicts order prefecture and circuit chief ministers to treat the people well; occasionally inner attendants are sent to inquire; supervisory commissioners are warned to inspect old, ill, and incompetent officials.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects were ordered to care for the people; inner attendants inquired; incompetent officials were inspected.

sentences.zh: 初，建隆三年，戶部郎中沈義倫使吳越還，言：“揚、泗饑民多死，郡中軍儲尚餘萬斛，宜以貸民。”

translations.literal: Earlier, in the third year of Jianlong, Ministry of Revenue Langzhong Shen Yilun, returning from an mission to Wu-Yue, said: "In Yang and Si, famine victims die in great numbers; the commandery still has more than ten thousand shi in military stores—it is fitting to lend the people."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianlong, Shen Yilun returning from Wu-Yue said: "Yang and Si famine victims die in multitudes while military stores hold ten thousand shi—it should be lent to the people."

sentences.zh: 有司沮之曰：“若來歲不稔，誰任其咎？”

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark The relevant office obstructed, saying: "If next year is not fertile, who bears the blame?"
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark Officials objected: "If next year fails, who bears blame?"

sentences.zh: 義倫曰：“國家以廩粟濟民，自當召和氣，致豐年，寧憂水旱耶？”

translations.literal: Yilun said: "The state uses granary grain to succor the people—of itself it should summon harmonious qi and bring a fertile year; why worry about flood and drought?"
translations.idiomatic: Yilun said: "Granary relief summons harmony and harvest—why fear drought?"

sentences.zh: 太祖悅而從之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark Emperor Taizu was pleased and followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark Emperor Taizu approved.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔州縣興復義倉，歲收二稅，石別收一斗，貯以備凶歉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict ordered prefectures and counties to restore charity granaries, each year collecting one dou per shi of the two taxes to store against famine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, prefectures restored charity granaries, collecting one dou per shi of the two taxes for famine reserve.

sentences.zh: 平廣南、江南，輒詔振其饑，其勤恤遠人，德意深厚。

translations.literal: Pacifying Lingnan and Jiangnan, they repeatedly issued an edict relief for their famine—their diligent care for distant people, virtuous intent deep and thick.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying Lingnan and Jiangnan, they repeatedly relieved famine—deep kindness to distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 太宗恭儉仁愛，諄諄勸民務農重穀，毋或妄費。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong was respectful, frugal, and benevolent, earnestly urging the people to farm and value grain, never wasting rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong was frugal and benevolent, urging farming and thrift.

sentences.zh: 是時惠民所積，不為無備，又置常平倉，乘時增糴，唯恐其不足。

translations.literal: At that time Beneficial stores were not without reserve; they also established Ever-Normal granaries, buying when timely to increase stores, fearing insufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Beneficial stores had reserves; Ever-Normal granaries bought grain lest stores run short.

sentences.zh: 真宗繼之，益務行養民之政，於是推廣淳化之製，而常平、惠民倉殆遍天下矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong succeeded and further pursued policies to nourish the people; thus he extended the Chunhua system and Ever-Normal and Beneficial granaries nearly covered the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong extended Chunhua policy until Ever-Normal and Beneficial granaries covered the realm.

sentences.zh: 仁宗、英宗一遇災變，則避朝變服，損膳徹樂。

translations.literal: Emperors Renzong and Yingzong, whenever disaster changed, avoided court, changed dress, reduced meals, and withdrew music.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Renzong and Yingzong, on disasters, avoided court, changed dress, and reduced meals.

sentences.zh: 恐懼修省，見於顏色；

translations.literal: Fearful self-examination and reform appeared in their countenance;
translations.idiomatic: Fear and repentance showed on their faces;

sentences.zh: 惻怛哀矜，形於詔旨。

translations.literal: compassionate grief appeared in edicts.
translations.idiomatic: compassion appeared in edicts.

sentences.zh: 慶曆初，詔天下復立義倉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingli, an edict ordered charity granaries restored throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingli's start, charity granaries were restored empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐二年，又詔天下置廣惠倉，使老幼疾貧者皆有所養。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiayou, another edict ordered Broad-Benefit granaries so the old, young, ill, and poor all had support.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiayou, Broad-Benefit granaries were ordered for the aged, young, ill, and poor.

sentences.zh: 累朝相承，其慮於民也既周，其施於民也益厚。

translations.literal: Successive courts inherited; concern for the people was thorough and benefits to the people ever thicker.
translations.idiomatic: Successive courts inherited these policies; care for the people grew ever deeper.

sentences.zh: 而又一時牧守，亦多得人，如張詠之治蜀，歲糶米六萬石，著之皇祐甲令。

translations.literal: Moreover, local governors of the time also often obtained good men—like Zhang Yong governing Shu, yearly selling sixty thousand shi of rice, recorded in the Huangyou A-order.
translations.idiomatic: Local governors often excelled—Zhang Yong in Shu sold sixty thousand shi yearly, recorded in the Huangyou regulations.

sentences.zh: 富弼之移青州，擇公私廬舍十餘萬區，散處流民以廩之，凡活五十餘萬人，募而為兵者又萬餘人，天下傳以為法。

translations.literal: Fu Bi moving to Qingzhou chose more than one hundred thousand public and private lodges, dispersing refugees to granary them—altogether saving more than five hundred thousand people; those recruited as soldiers were again more than ten thousand—throughout the realm it was transmitted as law.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi in Qingzhou lodged refugees in more than one hundred thousand buildings, saving five hundred thousand people and recruiting ten thousand soldiers—a model for the realm.

sentences.zh: 知鄆州劉夔發廩振饑，民賴全活者甚眾，盜賊衰止，賜詔褒美。

translations.literal: Liu Qi, prefect of Yunzhou, opened granaries to relieve famine; very many people were preserved alive; bandits declined and stopped; an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi of Yunzhou opened granaries; many lived; banditry ceased; the court praised him.

sentences.zh: 知越州趙抃揭榜於通衢，令民有米增價以糶，於是米商輻湊，越之米價頓減，民無饑死。

translations.literal: Zhao Bian, prefect of Yuezhou, posted placards on the main road ordering people with rice to sell at increased price—thus grain merchants gathered; Yue's rice price suddenly fell and people did not starve.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bian in Yuezhou posted notices inviting grain sales; merchants came; prices fell and none starved.

sentences.zh: 若是之政，不可悉書，故於先王救荒之法為略具焉。

translations.literal: Such policies cannot all be written; therefore in the former kings' famine-relief methods a summary is provided.
translations.idiomatic: Such policies are countless; here is a summary of ancient famine relief.

sentences.zh: 先是，仁宗在位，哀病者乏方藥，為頒《慶曆善救方》。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Renzong reigned, pitying the sick lacking prescriptions, he promulgated the Qingli Good-Relief Prescriptions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Renzong, pitying the sick without medicine, issued the Qingli Good-Relief Prescriptions.

sentences.zh: 知雲安軍王端請官為給錢和藥予民，遂行於天下。

translations.literal: Wang Duan, military prefect of Yun'an, requested the government give money to compound medicine for the people—thereafter it was implemented throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duan of Yun'an requested government-funded medicine for the people; the practice spread empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 嚐因京師大疫，命太醫和藥，內出犀角二本，析而視之。

translations.literal: Once because of a great epidemic in the capital, the court ordered Imperial Physicians to compound medicine; from the inner palace two rhinoceros horns were taken out and split to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: During a capital epidemic, Imperial Physicians compounded medicine; two rhinoceros horns from the inner palace were inspected.

sentences.zh: 其一通天犀，內侍李舜舉請留供帝服禦。

translations.literal: One was a heaven-piercing rhinoceros; inner attendant Li Shunju requested it be kept for the Emperor's imperial use.
translations.idiomatic: One was a heaven-piercing horn; attendant Li Shunju asked to reserve it for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“吾豈貴異物而賤百姓？”

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "How can I value strange things and slight the common people?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "How can I value curios above the people?"

sentences.zh: 竟碎之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark He finally smashed it.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark He had it destroyed.

sentences.zh: 又蠲公私僦舍錢十日。

translations.literal: They also remitted private and public rental money for ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Private and public rents were remitted ten days.

sentences.zh: 令太醫擇善察脈者，即縣官授藥，審處其疾狀予之，無使貧民為庸醫所誤，夭閼其生。

translations.literal: They ordered Imperial Physicians to select those good at pulse examination; county officials gave medicine, examining disease conditions before granting it, lest poor people be misled by quack doctors and cut short their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled physicians gave medicine through county officials so the poor were not harmed by quacks.

sentences.zh: 天禧中，於京畿近郊佛寺買地，以瘞死之無主者。

translations.literal: In the Tianxi period, near the capital suburbs in temple land they bought ground to bury the dead without masters.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxi, land near capital temples was bought to bury unclaimed dead.

sentences.zh: 瘞屍，一棺給錢六百，幼者半之；

translations.literal: For burying corpses, six hundred cash per coffin; for the young, half;
translations.idiomatic: Burial paid six hundred cash per coffin, half for children;

sentences.zh: 後不復給，死者暴露於道。

translations.literal: later payment ceased and the dead were exposed on roads.
translations.idiomatic: later payment ceased and corpses lay on roads.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐末，復詔給焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Jiayou, an edict again ordered payment.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiayou's end, payment was restored.

sentences.zh: 京師舊置東、西福田院，以廩老疾孤窮丐者，其後給錢粟者才二十四人。

translations.literal: The capital formerly established East and West Futian courts to granary the old, ill, solitary, poor, and beggars; afterward those given money and grain were only twenty-four persons.
translations.idiomatic: The capital's East and West Futian courts fed the destitute; later only twenty-four received grain.

sentences.zh: 英宗命增置南、北福田院，並東、西各廣官舍，日廩三百人。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong ordered addition of South and North Futian courts; East and West official quarters were all expanded, daily granarying three hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong added South and North Futian courts, feeding three hundred daily.

sentences.zh: 歲出內藏錢五百萬給其費，後易以泗州施利錢，增為八百萬。

translations.literal: Each year five million cash from the inner treasury supplied the expense; later changed to Sizhou profit money, increased to eight million.
translations.idiomatic: Five million inner treasury cash yearly later became eight million from Sizhou profits.

sentences.zh: 又詔：“州縣長吏遇大雨雪，蠲僦舍錢三日，歲毋過九日，著為令。”

translations.literal: Another edict: "When prefecture and county chiefs encounter great rain or snow, remit rental money three days; yearly not exceeding nine days—establish as regulation."
translations.idiomatic: Edict: prefects remit rent three days in heavy snow, nine days yearly maximum.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，京師雪寒，詔：“老幼貧疾無依丐者，聽於四福田院額外給錢收養，至春稍暖則止。”

translations.literal: In the second year of Xining, capital snow was bitterly cold; edict: "old, young, poor, ill without support may beyond Futian quota receive money for care until spring warms, then stop."
translations.idiomatic: Xining second year: destitute beyond Futian quota received winter care until spring.

sentences.zh: 九年，知太原韓絳言：“在法，諸老疾自十一月一日州給米豆，至次年三月終。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Han Jiang, prefect of Taiyuan, said: "By law, all old and ill from the first day of the eleventh month receive beans from the prefecture until the third month next year."
translations.idiomatic: Han Jiang of Taiyuan said: by law the old and ill received beans from the eleventh month to the third month.

sentences.zh: 河東地寒，乞自十月一日起支，至次年二月終止；

translations.literal: Hedong is cold; we beg disbursement from the first of the tenth month until the second month next year;
translations.idiomatic: Hedong is colder; disburse from the tenth month to the second month;

sentences.zh: 如有餘，即至三月終。”

translations.literal: if surplus remains, until the third month.
translations.idiomatic: if surplus remains, until the third month.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark Approved.

sentences.zh: 凡鰥、寡、孤、獨、癃老、疾廢、貧乏不能自存應居養者，以戶絕屋居之；

translations.literal: All widowers, widows, orphans, solitary, crippled old, disabled, poor and unable to support themselves who should be cared for dwell in extinct-household dwellings;
translations.idiomatic: Destitute widowers, orphans, disabled, and poor without support dwelled in extinct-household properties;

sentences.zh: 無，則居以官屋，以戶絕財產充其費，不限月。

translations.literal: if none, they dwell in official houses, using extinct-household property for expense, without monthly limit.
translations.idiomatic: if none, in official houses funded by extinct-household property without monthly limit.

sentences.zh: 依乞丐法給米豆；

translations.literal: They give rice and beans according to the beggar law;
translations.idiomatic: Rice and beans were given under the beggar law;

sentences.zh: 不足，則給以常平息錢。

translations.literal: If insufficient, then give Ever-Normal interest money.
translations.idiomatic: If insufficient, Ever-Normal interest money was provided.

sentences.zh: 崇寧初，蔡京當國，置居養院、安濟坊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongning, Cai Jing held power and established Residency-Care courts and Relief-Dispensing wards.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongning, Cai Jing established Residency-Care courts and Relief-Dispensing wards.

sentences.zh: 給常平米，厚至數倍。

translations.literal: Ever-Normal rice was given, thick to several times the amount.
translations.idiomatic: Ever-Normal grain was issued at several times the usual ration.

sentences.zh: 差官卒充使令，置火頭，具飲膳，給以衲衣絮被。

translations.literal: Official soldiers were assigned as attendants; fire-keepers were placed; meals were provided; padded garments and cotton quilts were given.
translations.idiomatic: Official soldiers served as staff; cooks were appointed; meals and padded clothing were supplied.

sentences.zh: 州縣奉行過當，或具帷帳，雇乳母、女使，糜費無藝，不免率斂，貧者樂而富者擾矣。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties over-implemented—some provided curtains, hired wet-nurses and maidservants, spending without limit, inevitably levying broadly; the poor were pleased while the rich were harassed.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials overspent on curtains, nurses, and servants, levying broadly—the poor benefited while the wealthy were harassed.

sentences.zh: 三年，又置漏澤園。

translations.literal: In the third year, Leak-Seep Gardens were also established.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Leak-Seep burial gardens were established.

sentences.zh: 初，神宗詔：“開封府界僧寺旅寄棺柩，貧不能葬，令畿縣各度官不毛地三五頃，聽人安厝，命僧主之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Shenzong issued an edict: "In the Kaifeng metropolitan zone, monasteries lodging coffins—those poor unable to bury—let each metropolitan county set aside three to five qing of unproductive government land, permitting people to inter; order monks to manage."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shenzong ordered metropolitan monasteries holding coffins of the poor to receive three to five qing of barren land per county for burial under monastic management.

sentences.zh: 葬及三千人以上，度僧一人，三年與紫衣；

translations.literal: When burials reach three thousand persons or more, ordain one monk; after three years grant purple robe;
translations.idiomatic: At three thousand burials one monk was ordained; after three years he received a purple robe;

sentences.zh: 有紫衣，與師號，更使領事三年，願復領者聽之。”

translations.literal: with purple robe, grant a master title; further let him lead affairs three years; those wishing to continue leading are permitted.
translations.idiomatic: with purple robe came a master title and three more years of leadership; renewal was permitted.

sentences.zh: 至是，蔡京推廣為園，置籍，瘞人並深三尺，毋令暴露，監司巡曆檢察。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark At this point Cai Jing extended it as gardens, established registers, buried people three chi deep so none were exposed; supervisory commissioners toured and inspected.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark Cai Jing extended this into registered gardens with three-foot burials and supervisory inspection.

sentences.zh: 安濟坊亦募僧主之，三年醫愈千人，賜紫衣、祠部牒各一道。

translations.literal: Relief-Dispensing wards also recruited monks to manage; healing one thousand persons in three years granted purple robe and one Ministry diploma each.
translations.idiomatic: Relief wards recruited monk managers; healing one thousand patients in three years earned purple robe and a Ministry diploma.

sentences.zh: 醫者人給手曆，以書所治痊失人，歲終考其數為殿最。

translations.literal: Each physician was given a hand register recording cures and failures; at year end the count determined excellence or failure.
translations.idiomatic: Physicians kept registers of cures and failures for annual evaluation.

sentences.zh: 諸城、砦、鎮、市戶及千以上有知監者，依各縣增置居養院、安濟坊、漏澤園。

translations.literal: Walled cities, stockades, garrisons, markets with one thousand households and above having supervisory officials—each county increased Residency-Care courts, Relief wards, and Leak-Seep gardens accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Cities, garrisons, and markets of one thousand households or more added Residency-Care courts, Relief wards, and Leak-Seep gardens.

sentences.zh: 道路遇寒僵仆之人及無衣丐者，許送近便居養院，給錢米救濟。

translations.literal: Those frozen on roads and beggars without clothes—permitted to send to the nearest Residency-Care court, giving money and rice for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Frozen corpses on roads and unclothed beggars were sent to the nearest Residency-Care court for money and rice.

sentences.zh: 孤貧小兒可教者，令入小學聽讀，其衣襴於常平頭子錢內給造，仍免入齋之用。

translations.literal: Orphaned poor children who can be taught—order them into elementary schools to listen and read; their clothing is made from Ever-Normal head-cloth money, still exempt from entering-hall expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Teachable orphan poor entered elementary school with clothing paid from Ever-Normal funds.

sentences.zh: 遺棄小兒，雇人乳養，仍聽宮觀、寺院養為童行。

translations.literal: Abandoned infants—hire people to nurse and rear; still permit palaces, temples, and monasteries to raise them as acolytes.
translations.idiomatic: Abandoned infants were nursed by hirelings or raised as temple acolytes.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年，詔：“居養、安濟、漏澤可參考元豐舊法，裁立中製。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuanhe, an edict: "Residency-Care, Relief, and Leak-Seep may reference Yuanfeng old law and establish a moderate system."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuanhe, Residency-Care, Relief, and Leak-Seep were ordered to follow Yuanfeng precedent at moderate scale.

sentences.zh: 應居養人日給粳米或粟米一升，錢十文省，十一月至正月加柴炭，五文省，小兒減半。

translations.literal: Those cared for daily receive one sheng of husked rice or grain and ten cash (standard); from the eleventh month to the first month add fuel coal, five cash (standard); children half.
translations.idiomatic: Residents received one sheng of rice and ten cash daily, plus winter fuel; children received half.

sentences.zh: 安濟坊錢米依居養法，醫藥如舊制。

translations.literal: Relief ward money and grain follow Residency-Care law; medicine as old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Relief ward funds followed Residency-Care rules; medicine followed old regulations.

sentences.zh: 漏澤園除葬埋依見行條法外，應資給若齋醮等事悉罷。”

translations.literal: Leak-Seep gardens—besides burial per current articles, all supplies such as fasting and sacrifices are abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Leak-Seep gardens provided burial only; fasting and sacrifice expenses were abolished.

sentences.zh: 高宗南渡，民之從者如歸市。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong crossed south, the people who followed were like returning to market.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong fled south, refugees followed like shoppers flooding a market.

sentences.zh: 既為之衣食以振其饑寒，又為之醫藥以救其疾病；

translations.literal: Having clothed and fed them to relieve hunger and cold, they also gave medicine to save their illnesses;
translations.idiomatic: They were clothed, fed, and given medicine;

sentences.zh: 其有隕於戈甲、斃於道路者，則給度牒瘞埋之。

translations.literal: those who fell to weapons or died on roads—donation diplomas were given for burial.
translations.idiomatic: those killed in war or on the road received diplomas for burial.

sentences.zh: 〈（若丐者育之於居養院；

translations.literal: (If beggars, rear them in Residency-Care courts;
translations.idiomatic: (Beggars were kept in Residency-Care courts;

sentences.zh: 其病也，療之於安濟坊；

translations.literal: if ill, treat them in Relief-Dispensing wards;
translations.idiomatic: the sick in Relief-Dispensing wards;

sentences.zh: 其死也，葬之於漏澤園，歲以為常。）〉

translations.literal: if dead, bury them in Leak-Seep gardens—yearly as constant.)
translations.idiomatic: the dead in Leak-Seep gardens—yearly as constant.)

sentences.zh: 紹興以來，歲有水旱，發常平義倉，或濟或糶或貸，如恐不及。

translations.literal: Since Shaoxing, every year there is flood or drought; Ever-Normal and charity granaries are opened, relieving, selling, or lending—as if fearing it is not enough.
translations.idiomatic: Since Shaoxing, annual floods and droughts opened Ever-Normal and charity granaries for relief, sale, and lending without stint.

sentences.zh: 然當艱難之際，兵食方急，儲蓄有限，而振給無窮，復以爵賞誘富人相與補助，亦權宜不得已之策也。

translations.literal: Yet in hard times military grain was urgent, stores limited while relief endless; again using rank rewards to induce the wealthy to assist was also an expedient measure of necessity.
translations.idiomatic: In hard times military grain was urgent and stores limited; rank rewards inducing wealthy assistance were necessary expedients.

sentences.zh: 二十八年夏，浙東、西田損於風水。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year summer, Zhe East and West fields were damaged by wind and water.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, summer wind and flood damaged Zhejiang fields.

sentences.zh: 在法，水旱及七分以上者振濟，詔自今及五分處亦振之。

translations.literal: By law, flood and drought of seven-tenths loss or more receive relief; edict from now also relieves at five-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: By law relief applied at seven-tenths crop loss; now five-tenths also qualified.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，詔諸處守臣撥常平義倉米二分振糶，臨安府撥樁積之米。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, an edict ordered local chiefs to allocate two-tenths of Ever-Normal and charity grain for relief sale; Lin'an used staked reserve rice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, local chiefs allocated two-tenths of Ever-Normal and charity grain for relief sale.

sentences.zh: 三十一年正月，雪寒，民多艱食。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year first month, snow was cold and the people had difficult food.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, first month, snow and cold left the people hungry.

sentences.zh: 詔臨安府並屬縣以常平米減時價之半，振糶十日；

translations.literal: Edict Lin'an prefecture and subordinate counties sell Ever-Normal grain at half the current price for relief sale ten days;
translations.idiomatic: Lin'an sold Ever-Normal grain at half price for ten days;

sentences.zh: 臨安府城內外貧乏之家，人給錢二百、米一斗及柴炭錢，並於內藏給之；

translations.literal: within and outside Lin'an city poor households—each person given two hundred cash, one dou rice, and fuel money, all from the inner treasury;
translations.idiomatic: poor households in Lin'an received two hundred cash, one dou rice, and fuel from the inner treasury;

sentences.zh: 〈（凡遇寒、遇暑、遇雨、遇火、遇赦及祈禱、即位、生辰、上尊號、生皇太子、晏駕、大祥之類，臨安之民暨三衙諸軍時有振恤，及放商稅、公私房賃。）〉

translations.literal: (Whenever cold, heat, rain, fire, amnesty, prayers, enthronement, birthdays, honorific titles, birth of imperial sons, imperial death, great mourning, and the like—Lin'an people and Three Yamen armies sometimes received relief, and commercial taxes and public-private rents were remitted.)
translations.idiomatic: (On cold, heat, rain, fire, amnesties, prayers, enthronements, birthdays, and mourning, Lin'an people and armies received relief and tax and rent remissions.)

sentences.zh: 輔郡之民，令諸州以常平錢依臨安府振之。

translations.literal: People of auxiliary prefectures—order all prefectures to relieve with Ever-Normal money following Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Auxiliary prefectures followed Lin'an's Ever-Normal relief.

sentences.zh: 孝宗隆興二年秋，霖雨害稼，出內帑銀四十萬兩，變糴以濟民。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longxing autumn, prolonged rain harmed crops; forty myriad taels of inner-coffers silver were released, exchanged for grain to succor the people.
translations.idiomatic: Longxing second year autumn rain ruined crops; forty myriad taels bought grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 乾道六年夏，振浙西被水貧民。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiandao summer, Zhe West flood victims were relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Qiandao sixth year summer relieved Zhe West flood victims.

sentences.zh: 七年八月，湖南、江西旱，立賞格以勸積粟之家。

translations.literal: In the seventh year eighth month, Hunan and Jiangxi drought—reward scales were established to encourage grain-storing households.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year of Qiandao, eighth month, Hunan and Jiangxi drought—rewards encouraged grain hoarders to sell.

sentences.zh: 〈（無官人：一千五百石補進義校尉，願補不理選艱將仕郎者聽；

translations.literal: (For men without office: one thousand five hundred shi supplements Advance Righteousness Corps commander; those wishing supplemental Irregular Gentleman without selection difficulty are permitted;
translations.idiomatic: (Men without office: 1,500 shi earned Advance Righteousness Corps commander;

sentences.zh: 二千石補進武校尉，進士與免文解一次，四千石補承信郎，進士與補上州文學；

translations.literal: two thousand shi supplements Advance Martial Corps commander, jinshi receives one civil exemption; four thousand shi supplements Trustworthy Gentleman, jinshi supplements upper-prefecture literary student;
translations.idiomatic: 2,000 shi earned Advance Martial Corps commander; 4,000 shi Trustworthy Gentleman;

sentences.zh: 五千石補承節郎，進士補迪功郎。

translations.literal: five thousand shi supplements Trustworthy Officer, jinshi supplements Di Gong Lang.
translations.idiomatic: 5,000 shi Trustworthy Officer.

sentences.zh: 文臣：一千石減二年磨勘，選人轉一官；

translations.literal: Civil officials: one thousand shi reduces two years merit review; selection candidates promote one rank;
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials: 1,000 shi reduced merit review two years;

sentences.zh: 二千石減三年磨勘，選人循一資，各與占射差遣一次；

translations.literal: two thousand shi reduces three years merit review, selection candidates advance one grade, each with one reserved dispatch;
translations.idiomatic: 2,000 shi three years; 3,000 shi one rank and two grades with dispatch;

sentences.zh: 三千石轉一官，選人循兩資，各與占射差遣一次。

translations.literal: three thousand shi promotes one rank, selection candidates advance two grades, each with one reserved dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: similar rewards for selection candidates.

sentences.zh: 武臣：一千石減二年磨勘，選人轉一資；

translations.literal: Martial officials: one thousand shi reduces two years merit review, selection candidates advance one grade;
translations.idiomatic: Martial officials: parallel rewards at 1,000–3,000 shi;

sentences.zh: 二千石減三年磨勘，選人循一資，各與占射差遣一次；

translations.literal: two thousand shi reduces three years merit review, selection candidates advance one grade, each with one reserved dispatch;
translations.idiomatic: two thousand shi: three-year merit reduction and one grade with dispatch;

sentences.zh: 三千石轉一官，選人循兩資，各與占射差遣一次。

translations.literal: three thousand shi promotes one rank, selection candidates advance two grades, each with one reserved dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: three thousand shi: one rank and two grades with dispatch.

sentences.zh: 五千石以上，文武臣並取旨優與推恩。）〉

translations.literal: five thousand shi and above—civil and martial officials all seek imperial decree for superior grace.)
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand shi and above: special grace by imperial order.)

sentences.zh: 九月，臣僚言：“諸路旱傷，請以檢放展閣責之運司，糶給借貸責之常平，覺察妄濫責之提刑，體量措置責之安撫。”

translations.literal: In the ninth month, officials said: "All circuits drought-damaged—please assign inspection, deferral, and extension to transport commissioners; relief sale, lending, and borrowing to Ever-Normal; detecting false abuse to judicial investigation; overall measures to pacification commissioners."
translations.idiomatic: Officials proposed dividing drought duties among transport, Ever-Normal, judicial, and pacification commissioners.

sentences.zh: 上諭宰執曰：“轉運司止今檢放，恐他日振濟不肯任責。”

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark The Emperor told the chief ministers: "Transport commissioners only inspect now—fearing that later they will not take responsibility for relief."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared transport commissioners would inspect but refuse relief responsibility.

sentences.zh: 虞允文奏曰：“轉運司主一路財賦，謂之省計。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark Yu Yunwen memorialized: "Transport commissioners manage one circuit's finances—called provincial accounts."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen said transport commissioners managed circuit finances called provincial accounts.

sentences.zh: 凡州郡有餘、不足，通融相補，正其責也。”

translations.literal: Where prefectures have surplus or shortfall, mutual adjustment is exactly their responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Balancing surplus and deficit across prefectures was their duty.

sentences.zh: 淳熙八年，詔：“去歲江、浙、湖北、淮西旱傷處已行振糴，其鰥寡孤獨貧不自存、無錢收糴者，濟以義米。”

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chunxi, an edict: "Last year Jiang, Zhe, Hubei, and Huai West drought places already had relief sale; for widowers, orphans, solitary, poor unable to support themselves without money to buy grain—succor with charity rice."
